verdicts.strongest_argument: Two things put this at the top of the scale. First, it restates published guidance: the $1.30-1.40bn revenue, $68-78m adjusted EBITDA and $310-320m net income figures and the $100m repurchase authorisation all come from the 2026-06-09 release, are in the stored body (docs/4b236ec1977fb78cc0d372d18adc6bc447a8957b.txt, snapshots/20260830T084126Z.json item 1, admissible per clean-view) and are in the 8-K items 2.02/7.01/9.01 in filings.json. Second, the finding's claim that 'nothing in the 88-item capture states it' is answered by its own independence field: Noble Capital Markets initiated coverage on 2026-06-18 with, in the hunter's words, 'precisely this thesis' - the WHP Global IP monetisation unlocking hidden brand value and the market underappreciating long-term earnings potential - published on channelchek. Published sell-side research asserting the exact conclusion is the strongest disproof of novelty available. Third, and most importantly, the arithmetic the finding calls unpriced is a category error. A $310-320m net income guide alongside a $68-78m adjusted EBITDA guide is a one-time, largely non-cash accounting gain from transferring the IP into the WHP structure - it is not distributable earnings and comparing it to a $365m market capitalisation as though the equity trades at 1.1x earnings is exactly the kind of arithmetic error the scale reserves its top band for. The operating business the market is capitalising is the $68-78m EBITDA line on declining revenue, which is precisely what the -41% from the high reflects. The buyback is real and large, but a $100m authorisation is an authorisation, not a completed retirement, and its existence has been public since June.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The event is a June price bar, and price bars are the most public object in this exercise. The close-to-close +8.47% is in the sealed baseline's own history, and the pre-market -5.8% is quoted in the admissible stored body (entry 2026-06-09T12:29:17Z) - so both halves are published, one in the baseline and one in the capture. The claim that the join 'is exactly the kind of two-source join nothing publishes' overstates the difficulty: a fourteen-point intraday reversal on the day of a results release is visible on any intraday chart of 2026-06-09 and is the sort of session that gets narrated in real time by the same stream the hunter is reading. The inference - that the marginal buyer at this price is not reacting to the revenue line - is one observation from one session three months ago, and the finding itself asks to have it collapsed into #0. There is also a sequencing problem: whatever the buyback did on 06-09, the stock is 11.9% lower over the last twenty sessions and 7.5% lower over the last five, so if a price-insensitive repurchase bid were the dominant force it is not visible in the recent tape.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the reachable-but-unconnected case and I score it there. Every accession is in filings.json with a date - two 8-Ks carrying item 5.02 on 06-30 and 07-10, an S-8 on 07-14, a Form 3 and Form 4 on 07-15, a 144 on 07-23 and two Form 4s on 08-04 - so an EDGAR reader had the whole sequence six weeks out, but no body is stored and nothing in the capture draws it together. What stops it going lower is exactly that quietness; what stops it going higher is that the sequence has an entirely ordinary reading. An 8-K item 5.02, followed four days later by an S-8 and then by a Form 3 from a new filer, is the standard paperwork of hiring an officer and registering the shares for their equity plan - the S-8 is the tell, because a departure does not require a new registration statement. Two 5.02 filings eleven days apart at a company mid-restructuring is unremarkable when one of them is plausibly a board change. The finding provides no name, no role and no size, and it correctly signs itself against the other two. Its own framing - 'the main thing that could make the guide unreliable' - is a conditional about a possibility, not a fact about the quarter.
